sources.quote: More than three decades after leaving elected office, a former South Carolina congressman transferred $1.25 million from his campaign reserves into a Morgan Stanley account for charitable giving.
sources.searcher_note: Reports the Oct 2024 $1.25M 'donation of securities' to a Morgan Stanley donor-advised fund from Tallon's committee, $96,500 left, 2024 year-end report filed late; the core of the lead's 2024-cycle payout. Page returns 403 to WebFetch; text read via a direct browser-agent download.

sources.quote: But his decade in Congress left him with more than $400,000 in his campaign account. He kept it open, then invested the money, turning it into $1 million.
sources.searcher_note: Earliest found coverage of Tallon's dormant committee; same piece is the pattern story: roughly 100 zombie campaigns that spent more than $20 million since 1995.

sources.quote: Robin Tallon is the poster child for the problems with zombie campaigns, former officeholders leaving their campaign accounts open for decades and using them as informal retirement funds
sources.searcher_note: Local TV follow-up; account over $1M as of April 2018 FEC filing; Campaign Legal Center quote.

notes: Tallon's committee and its 2024 payout (the $1.25M Morgan Stanley transfer) are covered by name in SC Daily Gazette, April 2025; the lead's exact $1,391,737 total and the $0-from-individuals detail were not found in any source. No source found for the aggregate (139 committees for races run by 2016 holding $7.98M, median $366, 3 hold 59%); closest pattern coverage is Tampa Bay Times 2018 (~100 zombie campaigns, $20M+ spent since 1995). A search snippet said Tallon is running for the 2026 SC Senate seat as an independent, citing Wikipedia, but the fetched Wikipedia pages did not contain that text, so it is not recorded. No coverage dated after 2026-06-30 found for Tallon. Bloomberg Government 'Attacking the Undead' page returned 403 and was not recorded.
